ideas.title: Prompt A/B Lab
ideas.summary: A minimal web app to run two AI prompts side by side, highlighting exactly where their outputs diverge, with local experiment history.
ideas.description: A minimal web app where you write two versions of an AI prompt, fire them at the same model simultaneously, and see the outputs side by side with inline diff highlighting showing exactly where they diverge. Experiment history is saved to localStorage so you can compare across sessions.
keyFeatures: Dual-pane editor: write Prompt A and Prompt B, choose model and temperature
Side-by-side output view with character-level diff highlighting
Experiment history saved locally (prompt pairs + outputs + timestamps)
One-click copy of winning prompt to clipboard
ideas.techStack: React + Vite, Tailwind CSS, Claude API or Gemini API, diff2html or custom diff logic, localStorage
ideas.whyInteresting: Prompt engineering is still mostly trial-and-error in a single chat window; this makes it systematic and visual, which is exactly the kind of sharp single-purpose tool that shows strong product thinking in a portfolio.
ideas.inspiredBy: Hacker News 'What are you working on? (June 2026)' threads and discussions around agentic coding workflows

ideas.title: Exit Ticket Bot
ideas.summary: Paste your lecture notes, get 3 AI-generated quiz questions, show a QR code, and see a live concept-weakness heatmap as students answer on their phones.
ideas.description: A web dashboard where an instructor pastes lecture notes or slide text, and the tool instantly generates 3 short quiz questions. A QR code appears on screen; students scan it on their phones and answer in under 2 minutes. The teacher sees a live results dashboard plus an AI summary identifying which concepts the class is weakest on, ready to use at the start of the next lecture.
keyFeatures: AI question generation from pasted lecture text (multiple-choice + short-answer)
Shareable QR code that opens a zero-install mobile answer form
Real-time answer aggregation via Supabase realtime subscriptions
Post-class concept weakness summary generated by Claude
ideas.techStack: React + Vite, Tailwind CSS, Supabase (realtime + database), Claude API, qrcode.react
ideas.whyInteresting: Closing the feedback loop after class normally requires clicker hardware or a third-party subscription; this replaces both with a free self-hosted tool while adding AI-powered diagnosis of which specific concepts need revisiting.
ideas.inspiredBy: iClicker real-time feedback loops and Deck.Toys adaptive learning paths (edcafe.ai AI classroom tools roundup, June 2026)

ideas.title: AI Podcast Studio
ideas.summary: Students build an app that turns any CS topic into a scripted two-voice podcast dialogue, synthesizes it with TTS, and delivers a downloadable MP3.
ideas.description: Students build a web app that takes a CS topic chosen by the user and generates a realistic 5-10 minute podcast episode as a scripted dialogue between two AI personas: a curious beginner and a pragmatic senior developer. A TTS API converts the script to audio, which can be played in-browser or downloaded as an MP3.
keyFeatures: Topic picker with difficulty slider (intro / intermediate / advanced)
LLM generates a structured two-voice dialogue script with natural transitions
TTS synthesis of each voice (distinct voices for each persona)
In-browser audio player with transcript toggle, plus MP3 download
ideas.techStack: React + Vite, Flask or FastAPI backend, Claude API (script generation), ElevenLabs API or browser Web Speech API (TTS), ffmpeg (audio merging)
ideas.whyInteresting: The project teaches an end-to-end AI pipeline (LLM prompt chaining, TTS, audio I/O, UX) and produces a genuinely useful artifact: an on-demand audio explainer students can listen to while commuting, with real production-quality engineering challenges around latency and voice consistency.
ideas.inspiredBy: VoxCPM2 (tokenizer-free multilingual TTS) trending on GitHub in June 2026, and the broader rise of AI-generated audio as a learning medium
